newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 19.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

WASHINGTON - A long-time officer of the CIA's clandestine operations service was charged by federal authorities with passing an unknown quantity of national secrets to Russia over the past two years for cash payments of around $120,000.
WASHINGTON - Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening has decided to propose a cut in personal income taxes to improve the state's business climate.
WASHINGTON - Senior U.S. officials have tentatively concluded that the international security force proposed by Canada to aid Rwandan refugees in Zaire is no longer needed.

WASHINGTON - American companies and their European counterparts have bought up failed state-owned enterprises and ancient cigarette factories across Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, laying the foundation for a Western-owned tobacco industry in a vast market.
WASHINGTON - Caffeinated water, or "spring water with an attitude", is being marketed by at least four companies.

WASHINGTON - The passengers and crew of ValuJet Flight 592 knew they were in trouble almost two minutes before the jet crashed into the Florida Everglades last May, and one man even used his cellular phone to make one last call to his wife.
